rv.q: All of that leads me to say that "Leopoldstadt," including this production of "Leopoldstadt," is essential viewing for any Stoppard fan, for anyone Jewish, certainly, but also anyone looking at how one of the English language's sexiest, smartest, shiniest writer-celebrities finally found his way home, writing how he wanted to exit, as he did...

Instead, “Leopoldstadt” receives its Chicago-area premiere at the intimate Writers Theatre in suburban Glencoe, under the direction of esteemed Stoppard collaborator Carey Perloff, in a lavish, captivating, meet-the-artistic-moment production populated by a who’s who of local actors.

As I left the theater, I was touched by the fact that in writing this play, Stoppard was doing what so many of us do when we go to the theater: Process questions of identity and history and how to make sense of the world through art.
The audience seemed to be applauding not merely a production, but a masterpiece.

As these three come to agree on the importance of keeping alive the memories of those who did not survive and of the unspeakable crimes committed against them, they draw the audience into the same compact.
This is a must-see production that requires more than one viewing due to its complexity, depth, and impact.

With this breathtaking, must-see presentation of Tom Stoppard’s sweeping epic tragicomedy, Writers Theatre once again shows why it’s consistently regarded as one of the brightest jewels in Chicago’s theatrical crown.
Directed by Carey Perloff, a longtime friend and collaborator of Stoppard’s, this final stage play proves to be among his best.
The play is a fitting swansong for one of the masters of theatrical storytelling.
Writers Theatre’s stellar Midwest premiere of Tom Stoppard’s Tony Award-winning “Leopoldstadt” marks another triumph for the Glencoe theater.
Ultimately, Stoppard looked to himself for answers, and in a sense, that's what we all must do after watching Leopoldstadt .
“Leopoldstadt” is a valuable resource for anyone trying to understand the world through the eyes of a people who have seen it all and persevere.
The history it tackles is currently being denied by wide swaths of the population—which makes the challenging, engaging drama all the more important.
Leopoldstadt is a compelling play but can be difficult to follow because there are so many characters and so many topics under discussion.
Leopoldstadt, now on stage at Writers Theatre , is one of those rare theatrical experiences.

cn.t: Critics praise Stoppard's final play as a powerful, sweeping family saga that brings Jewish history to life with intellectual depth and emotional resonance. The ambitious production dazzles with its stellar ensemble cast and masterful storytelling.
